### How to spot critical changes between the two PDFs

A direct comparison of the binary files (`diff`, `cmp`) will almost always flag everything as different because even trivial metadata updates alter the underlying bytes. To focus on substantive content changes—especially around the “budget analysis” portion—you’ll typically take the following steps:

| Stage | Action | Why it matters |
|-------|--------|---------------|
| **Extract Text** | Convert each PDF to plain text (`pdftotext`, `pdfminer.six`, `qpdf --extract-text`, etc.). | Removes compression & formatting; gives us searchable, comparable text. |
| **Locate Sections** | Grep for `"budget analysis"` (case‑insensitive) in the extracted texts. Capture surrounding context (±5–10 lines). | Isolates the exact paragraph(s)/table(s) that matter. |
| **Diff the Blocks** | Run `diff` or `git diff` on the captured blocks. | Highlights additions/deletions/replacements word‑wise. |
| **Interpret Results** | Review flagged lines for quantitative shifts (numbers, percentages) or qualitative wording changes. | Determines whether adjustments affect financial conclusions or policy statements. |

#### Example workflow (Linux shell)

```sh
cd temp
mkdir txt
pdftotext final_report.pdf   txt/final.txt
pdftotext previous_report.pdf txt/past.txt

# Grab budget-analysis snippets
sed -n '/budget analysis/,+15p' txt/final.txt > txt/final_budget.txt
sed -n '/budget analysis/,+15p' txt/past.txt     > txt/past_budget.txt

# Diff the excerpts
diff -u txt/past_budget.txt txt/final_budget.txt > txt/budget_diff.patch
less txt/budget_diff.patch          # review changes
```

> **Note:** If the PDFs include scanned images rather than selectable text, OCR (Optical Character Recognition) via tools like Tesseract will be required before extraction works reliably.
